clue.text: Loud Verdi composition full of fire and passion

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction meaning loud

indicators.note: a composition puts things together in a new order, so the name is rearranged

explanation.surface: A rousing Verdi opera bursts with fire and passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loud' looks like it describes the opera, but it is the musical forte, and 'composition' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Fervid is a synonym of ardent, burning with intense feeling.

clue.text: Bolts from arguments

definitions.meaning: crossbow bolts are called ..., from their square heads

explanation.definitionFit: A crossbow bolt is a quarrel, and so is a bitter disagreement.

clue.text: They grip and hold on in the last resort

indicators.note: the shuffled letters hold the next word, taking it inside them
read as re-sort, to sort again, so the letters of the word last are rearranged

explanation.surface: People who cling on when all else fails.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'resort' as re-sort, to sort again: that is the anagram signal, giving TALS, which 'hold' wraps round the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird of prey's claws are what it grips its prey with.

clue.text: In which to see ring fighters

definitions.text: In which to see ring fighters

parts.words: In which to see ring fighters
parts.note: the boxing-ring picture hides a bullring where matadors fight bulls

explanation.definitionFit: A corrida is a Spanish bullfight, held in a ring where the fighters appear.

clue.text: Jellyfish in sea north of America

parts.note: the Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea
USA is the United States of America

explanation.surface: A jellyfish found in waters lying north of America.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'north of' puts MED above USA.
explanation.definitionFit: Medusa is the zoological term for the free-swimming bell-shaped form of a jellyfish.

clue.text: Rather like a chat about a change of weather

indicators.note: the reshuffled letters go about, surrounding, the single letter
a change of the word weather means its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something resembling small talk about the weather turning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of' rearranges WEATHER into WHEATER, and 'about' puts it round A. A chat is a small songbird, not a conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: The wheatear is a small songbird of the chat family, so it is much like a chat.

clue.text: Losing head, gambler becomes an embezzler

indicators.note: losing its head means the synonym drops its first letter

parts.note: a speculator gambles on markets

explanation.surface: A gambler who loses his head turns to embezzling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing head' takes the first letter off SPECULATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A peculator is one who steals funds entrusted to them, an embezzler.

clue.text: I held wrong capital

indicators.note: held wrong, the letters are put in a mistaken order

explanation.surface: A confession that one's view was mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges the letters of I HELD.
explanation.definitionFit: Delhi, through New Delhi, is the capital city of India.

clue.text: No longer with the directors, taken to drink

definitions.meaning: read as over, finished, with the board of directors
thrown off a ship into the sea, which crosswords call the drink

explanation.definitionFit: Over the board means done with the directors; falling over the side of a ship lands one in the sea.

clue.text: Being liable to error

definitions.meaning: fallible, as in to err is ...

explanation.definitionFit: A person is a living creature, and people are fallible by nature.

clue.text: Hairstyle for a transformation?

indicators.note: a transformation changes the form of the two short words, rearranging them

explanation.surface: Which hairdo would suit a makeover?
explanation.definitionFit: The Afro is a rounded, bushy natural hairstyle.

clue.text: Intermediate gears none would wish to engage

definitions.meaning: idler gears sit between driving and driven gears
lazy people no employer wants to hire

explanation.definitionFit: Idler wheels transmit motion between gears, and loafers are workers nobody wants to take on.

clue.text: Beaten by heroic exploit in action

indicators.note: the exploit goes in, inside, the act

parts.note: a deed is an act
a feat is a bold deed

explanation.surface: Overcome by a hero's daring stunt in battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Defeated is a synonym of beaten, overcome in a contest.

clue.text: Graduates meeting shortly? It's in the wind

parts.note: BAs are Bachelors of Arts, holders of a first degree
soon means before long

explanation.surface: Graduates meeting soon? Word is getting around.
explanation.walkthrough: The wind is the woodwind section of an orchestra, not rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: The bassoon is a double-reed member of the orchestra's woodwind section.

clue.text: Daughter eschews flirting for marriage

indicators.note: to eschew is to avoid, so the letter is left out

parts.note: dalliance is casual amorous play

explanation.surface: A daughter gives up flirting and settles for marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance can be a union by marriage between families.

clue.text: Means of propulsion on a Roman ship, originally

indicators.note: originally points to the first letters of each word

explanation.surface: How a Roman galley was driven through the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' takes the first letters of ON A ROMAN SHIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowers drive a boat with these long-bladed poles.

clue.text: Unruly mob in Shakespeare use guns

indicators.note: an unruly crowd is out of order, so its letters are disordered

parts.note: the Bard is Shakespeare's nickname

explanation.surface: A riotous crowd in a Shakespeare play turns to firearms.
explanation.definitionFit: To bombard is to attack with artillery fire.

clue.text: Spread around, by the perimeter

indicators.note: spread out, the letters are scattered and laid out anew

explanation.surface: Something laid out round a border.
explanation.definitionFit: A boundary is the line marking the outer edge of an area.

clue.text: A rugby player, too fat to be fit

parts.note: a prop is a front-row forward in rugby
OS is outsize, clothing for the larger figure

explanation.surface: A rugby forward too heavy to be fit to play.
explanation.walkthrough: A prop is a front-row forward in rugby; OS (outsize) is a British clothing size label.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos means appropriate, suited to the occasion.

clue.text: Approve of gin? Nonsense!

parts.note: to clap is to applaud, showing approval
a gin is a snare or trap for game

explanation.surface: A question about endorsing a spirit, answered with scorn.
explanation.walkthrough: Gin here is a snare, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is pretentious empty talk, rubbish.

clue.text: Collect rands clutched by one who is settling up

indicators.note: the letter is held inside the person paying

parts.note: a payer is one who settles a bill
R is the abbreviation for the rand, South Africa's currency

explanation.surface: Someone paying up gathers his rand coins.
explanation.walkthrough: A collect is a short prayer in church liturgy, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: In church services a collect is a brief set prayer for the day.

clue.text: Aintree starter

definitions.meaning: Aintree, near Liverpool, is the racecourse that hosts the Grand National
the first dish of a meal

explanation.definitionFit: Aintree is a racing venue, and a starter is the first part of a meal.

clue.text: Spotless tea set put out

parts.note: cha is informal British slang for tea

indicators.note: put out of order, the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clean tea service laid out.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotless in the moral sense of pure, virtuous.

clue.text: Absorbing example of marine life

parts.note: absorbing looks like fascinating, but describes a sea creature that soaks up water

explanation.definitionFit: Sea sponges are simple marine animals whose porous bodies soak up liquid.

clue.text: Prohibition, most of all, is boring

parts.note: a ban forbids something

indicators.note: most of the word means its last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Prohibition, above all things, is dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the last letter of ALL to give AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Banal means trite and dull; the definition says the answer describes it.

clue.text: Fight and row, never sleeping together

parts.note: to box is to fight with fists
taken as written
to cox is to steer a rowing boat

explanation.surface: A fight and a quarrel: a couple who never share a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Box and Cox is a Victorian farce whose two lodgers share one room, one by day and one by night, so they never meet.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes two people taking turns, never present at the same time, after the farce's lodgers.

clue.text: Propeller guard

definitions.meaning: a ship's ... drives it through water
British prison slang for a warder

explanation.definitionFit: A ship's propeller is also called a screw, and prison slang uses the same word for a warder.

clue.text: Drink time — get the carriage

parts.note: porter is a dark beer
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A pint, then it's time to fetch the coach.
explanation.definitionFit: Porterage is the carrying of goods, or the charge for it.
